elements.element: Cap applies mutually to both parties
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED"

elements.element: Cap limb (a): fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"

elements.element: Cap limb (b): USD 1,000,000 floor, on a greater-of basis
elements.evidence: "EXCEED THE GREATER OF fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim AND USD 1,000,000"
"neither party shall be liable for any indirect or consequential damages"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "The foregoing limitation does not apply to Excluded Claims"; "a party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for data protection obligations
elements.evidence: "its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations, meaning Client's payment obligations under this Agreement, are not damages for cap purposes"
cap is "THE GREATER OF fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim AND USD 1,000,000", not a bare 12 months' fees cap

elements.element: Carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct"; "confidentiality ... obligations"

reasons: All atomic preferred elements are present: mutual cap, greater-of limbs with the exact fee basis and claim anchor plus the USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, the full uncapped carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP), and the payment-obligations statement.

Edits are confined to the liability sentence plus one concise inserted sentence set; the Section 12(a) indemnity and all other paragraphs are untouched, so unrelated commercial terms remain effective.

The retained original parenthetical "(OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT)" now overlaps with the Excluded Claims definition; harmless surplus (it is original text and the Excluded Claims list is mutual), but could be deleted for tidiness.

The gloss "Customer's payment obligations, meaning Client's payment obligations under this Agreement" avoids an undefined "Customer" term rather than creating one, so no dangling definition is introduced; it is slightly wordy but self-curing.

Fallback is not independently satisfied on its literal cap term (greater-of rather than 12 months' fees), which is immaterial because the locked target is preferred and the greater-of cap is more favourable to us.
